name: Miami
dek: Miami International Airport, WMO 72202. Wet from May through October.
paragraphs: The station is Miami International Airport, WMO 72202, height 9 m, position 25°47′26″N, 80°18′59″W. Miami Beach is not a separate file in this collection.

The highest average high in the table is 32.6 °C, in July and August. The lowest average low is 16.1 °C, in January. The wettest month by the precipitation column is June, at 266.9 mm, and the driest is January, at 46.6 mm.

climate.caption: Station: Miami International Airport, WMO 72202.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. Monthly values are copied as printed, with leading spaces removed; a value printed with no leading zero, such as -.3, is shown as -0.3.
climate.sourceTitle: WMO climate normals 1991-2020, Miami International Airport (72202)

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type A and B, 120 V, 60 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows United States at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page did not return the list, so the archive is the copy that was read.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: Section 316.081(1) of the Florida Statutes, on the Florida Senate site, says that on all roadways of sufficient width a vehicle shall be driven on the right half of the roadway, with exceptions such as overtaking, obstructions, three-lane roads, and one-way roads.

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.detail: Visit The USA, run by Brand USA, says diners usually tip 15–20% for a sit-down meal and 10% at a buffet, and that some restaurants add a gratuity for parties of six or more. Its same answer gives bartenders $1 a drink or 15–20%, taxis 10–18%, bell staff $1–2 a bag, housekeeping $2–5 a night, and tour guides 10–20%. It is guidance, not a law.
tipping.sourceTitle: Visit The USA (Brand USA), Travel Trade FAQ

water.label: Tap water
water.value: Safe to drink, per Visit The USA
water.detail: Visit The USA, run by Brand USA, says: "Protected by federal law, water in the United States is safe to drink." This is the tourism body's line, not a CDC or EPA statement, and local advisories can still apply.
water.sourceTitle: Visit The USA (Brand USA), Travel Trade FAQ

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the US Dollar, code USD, for the United States of America. It also lists US Dollar (Next day), code USN, a funds code, which is not printed as the currency.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab gives the United States 29 rows. America/New_York is commented Eastern (most areas). The other US rows are not collapsed into it.

entry.label: Official entry requirements
entry.note: CBP's page for international visitors. It applies to travelers arriving from outside the United States. We do not restate a visa rule.
